name: Contiv-VPP
what_it_is: A Kubernetes CNI plugin that uses FD.io VPP (Vector Packet Processing) as the userspace data plane to provide high-performance pod-to-pod, host-to-pod, and external-to-pod networking. It replaces kube-proxy by implementing Kubernetes services and network policies entirely within VPP, leveraging DPDK for fast NIC access.
components: contiv-vswitch (VPP data plane + Contiv VPP Agent control plane, runs on every node)
contiv-ksr (Kubernetes State Reflector — mirrors k8s API into ETCD)
contiv-etcd (dedicated ETCD instance for cluster state and VPP config persistence)
contiv-cni (CNI binary that forwards add/del pod requests via gRPC to contiv-vswitch)
contiv-stn (Steal-The-NIC daemon for single-NIC node deployments)
contiv-crd (Custom Resource Definition handler + netctl CLI for topology validation and runtime inspection)
contiv-ui (optional web UI with REST proxy for cluster visualization)
protocols: SRv6 / Segment Routing IPv6 (alternative inter-node transport and service chaining)
gRPC (CNI requests from kubelet to contiv-vswitch; STN requests)
VPP binary API over shared memory via GoVPP
DPDK (NIC binding for VPP data plane)
TAP interfaces v2 (pod-to-VPP and host-to-VPP connectivity)
memif (high-speed shared-memory interfaces for pod-to-pod service chaining)
measurement: HTTP REST endpoint on contiv-vswitch at 0.0.0.0:9999 (vpp-agent stats and debug)
Telemetry polling interval configurable (default 30s, can be disabled)
KVScheduler transaction history with configurable age limit (default 60 min)
Event history recording on contiv-agent with permanent init-period recording
contiv-netctl CLI for live IPAM assignments and VPP state inspection
configuration: contiv.conf ConfigMap: nodeToNodeTransport, useTAPInterfaces, tapInterfaceVersion, MTU (default 1450), NAT, GSO, STNVersion, enablePacketTrace

ipamConfig: podSubnetCIDR (default 10.1.0.0/16), podSubnetOneNodePrefixLen (default /24), vppHostSubnetCIDR (172.30.0.0/16), nodeInterconnectCIDR (192.168.16.0/24), nodeInterconnectDHCP, vxlanCIDR (192.168.30.0/24)
SRv6 IPAM CIDRs: servicePolicyBSIDSubnetCIDR, serviceNodeLocalSIDSubnetCIDR, nodeToNodePodLocalSIDSubnetCIDR, sfcPolicyBSIDSubnetCIDR, etc.
controller.conf: retry policy, resync deadlines, periodic healing interval, remote DB probing interval
Node-specific config via CRD (IP address, default gateway per node)
bolt.conf: persistent VPP config storage path and file mode
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework found in the repository
reboot-monkey.sh in vagrant/ directory suggests node reboot chaos testing capability
KVSCHED_VERIFY_MODE env var (commented out in deployment YAML) enables KVScheduler verification mode for debugging
modes: Dual-NIC mode (default): one NIC managed by DPDK/VPP for data plane, one NIC for k8s control plane
Single-NIC / STN (Steal-The-NIC) mode: one NIC shared between VPP data plane and host via TAP
SRv6 inter-node transport (alternative, useSRv6ForServices / useDX6ForSrv6NodetoNodeTransport flags)
Calico-VPP hybrid mode: some nodes run plain Calico, others run Calico with VPP
constraints: Requires DPDK-compatible NIC on each node for the VPP data plane interface; that NIC is invisible to the Linux host network stack
In dual-NIC mode each node must have at least 2 network interfaces; single-NIC STN mode trades NIC control complexity for fewer interfaces
VPP runs entirely in userspace and requires hugepage memory allocation on the host
ETCD must be healthy for VPP agents to receive configuration; loss of ETCD connectivity stalls control-plane updates (remoteDBProbingInterval default 3s)
Node ID-based IPAM means pod and VXLAN IP addresses are derived from node order; changing node IDs or reusing them after node removal may cause address conflicts
MTU is set to 1450 by default to accommodate VXLAN encapsulation overhead; mismatched MTU causes silent packet drops
Kubernetes network policies and services are enforced inside VPP — no fallback to iptables/kube-proxy; misconfigured VPP rules drop traffic without Linux-level visibility
notable_absences: No docker-compose file found; the project is Kubernetes-native and ships only Kubernetes YAML manifests and Vagrant-based local cluster definitions
No built-in load testing or traffic generation tooling in the repository
No Helm chart in the main repository (Helm templates are used to render the YAML but the chart itself is not published here)
No integrated distributed tracing (e.g., Jaeger/Zipkin) for VPP data-plane flows
